sentiment.label: risk_on
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-on grazie ai dati positivi sul PIL e alla riduzione delle tensioni geopolitiche. Il VIX è sceso sotto 20 e l'S&P 500 è in rialzo dell'1.75%. L'oro è in aumento del 3.74%, mentre il petrolio è in calo del 4.34%.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-on due to positive economic data and reduced geopolitical tensions. VIX dropped below 20 and S&P 500 is up 1.75%. Gold is up 3.74%, while oil is down 4.34%.

market_impact_summary.it: I mercati azionari sono in rialzo, con l'S&P 500 che guadagna l'1.75% e il VIX che scende sotto 20. Il dollaro USA è debole, con il DXY in calo dello 0.20%. I tassi di interesse sono in calo, con il TLT che guadagna l'1.30%.
market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets are up, with S&P 500 gaining 1.75% and VIX dropping below 20. US dollar is weak, with DXY down 0.20%. Interest rates are down, with TLT up 1.30%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 2.81%, Shanghai in rialzo dell'1.12%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dell'1.75%, il VIX è sceso del 4.53%. Il DXY è in calo dello 0.2%, a 99.66 L'oro è in rialzo del 3.74%, a $4243.3 l'oncia. Il petrolio è in calo del 4.34%, a $86.46 Il rendimento del decennale USA è in calo dell'1.74%, al 4.46%. Il BTP 10Y italiano è stabile al 3.73%.

La BCE è pronta a rialzare i tassi di nuovo, secondo il capo della Bundesbank. Questo potrebbe avere un impatto sui mercati europei. La situazione in Ucraina continua a essere monitorata, con sfide fiscali e finanziarie per il paese.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin guadagna l'1,51%, portandosi a 63.799 dollari. I flussi degli ETF mostrano un deflusso di 5,3 milioni di dollari. Il movimento rialzista di Bitcoin sembra non essere influenzato dalle recenti notizie sull'inflazione e sulla chiusura dello stretto di Hormuz.

Per quanto riguarda le altcoin, Ethereum sale dell'1,44% a mille 681 dollari, Solana guadagna il 2,87% a 67,19 dollari e BNB aumenta dell'1,18% a 606,67 dollari.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 12, in zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 2.81%, Shanghai up 1.12%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed up 1.75%, the VIX fell 4.53%. The DXY is down 0.2%, at 99.66 Gold is up 3.74%, at $4,243.3 per ounce. Oil is down 4.34%, at $86.46 The 10-year US yield is down 1.74%, to 4.46%. The Italian 10Y BTP is stable at 3.73%. The ECB is set to raise rates again, according to the head of the Bundesbank. This could have an impact on European markets. The situation in Ukraine continues to be monitored, with fiscal and financial challenges for the country. No major macroeconomic data due today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin gains 1.51%, moving to $63,799 ETF flows show an outflow of $5.3 million. The bullish move in Bitcoin seems to be unaffected by recent news on inflation and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Regarding altcoins, Ethereum rises 1.44% to $1,681, Solana gains 2.87% to $67.19 and BNB increases 1.18% to $606.67 The Fear & Greed Index is at 12, in Extreme Fear zone, suggests caution on investors. No macro data on the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles on our platform in the Top Stories section. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Raising Interest Rates Won’t Stabilize African Inflation
articles.snippet: Monetary tightening in Africa would not only fail to rein in inflation; it would raise the cost of productive investment, suppress growth, and hamper the continent's much-needed structural transformation. A better strategy would focus on accelerating this transformation by channeling finance into productive industries.

articles.snippet: As it faces the exigencies of an existential war, Ukraine is confronted with stark fiscal and financial policy trade-offs, despite the mitigation provided by large-scale external financial support. What is the broad fiscal equation for Ukraine looking forward, taking into account uncertainties about European funding beyond 2027? Can domestic revenue be raised? articles.title: Defence Investment Paralysis: Why the UK’s defence minister quit, and what it means
articles.snippet: Defence Investment Paralysis: Why the UK’s defence minister quit, and what it means Audio sseth.drupal@c… 11 June 2026 In this week’s episode of Independent Thinking, our experts discuss the UK’s defence funding crisis and Europe’s struggle to coordinate its rearmament effort. A tumultuous week for Britain’s faltering rearmament plans sees defence secretary John Healey resign from Keir Starmer’s cabinet, saying the prime minister and the Treasury lack the will to properly fund the defence of the nation. Al Carns, the armed forces minister, also resigned saying the government’s long-awaited Defence Investment Plan (DIP) was ‘not built for the threat we face’. The departures raise further questions over whether the DIP can address the costs and trade-offs involved in strengthening UK defence

articles.title: Oil Prices Tumble 4% on Iran Peace Optimism
articles.snippet: Oil prices plunged by more than 4% early on Friday as the market hopes the U.S. and Iran have made progress toward a peace deal. As of morning trade in Europe, the international benchmark, Brent Crude, had slipped by 4.34% at $86.36, extending the losses from Thursday when U.S. President Donald Trump called off a strike on Iran, claiming that a deal had been reached. The U.S. benchmark, WTI Crude, had dipped by 4.47% at $83.88. Both benchmarks were headed to a three-month low amid one of the most optimistic signals about a deal coming from the…

articles.title: Why Household Batteries Are Becoming Strategic Assets
articles.snippet: The Strait of Hormuz has become the pressure point of the global energy system. The war has already deprived global markets of 1 billion barrels of crude oil and petroleum products. For governments, part of the answer to this strategic crisis may now begin much closer to home.
